architecture.principle: Post and lintel. Timber, brick, plaster, sandstone. If a frame contains a true arch, a dome or marble, it is wrong.

construction.structure: timber posts, carved brackets, heavy beams; mud-brick and lime plaster; sandstone floors, steps, plinths
construction.openings: pierced lattice screens of wood or stone (jālī); rectangular doorways, sometimes corbelled
construction.interiors: low furniture only — floor seating, low stools, a dais. Brass oil lamps on stands. Undyed cotton drapes, unpatterned. Earth-pigment painted plaster, restrained.

never: anything Mughal, Rajput-palace, Victorian or fantasy-castle

cloth.principle: Cloth is woven, cut from the loom, and DRAPED. It is not tailored, not fitted, not buttoned. This single fact removes most anglicisation before a character is named.

garments.name: antarīya
garments.how: lower cloth, wrapped and tucked at the waist; length by rank and activity

garments.name: uttarīya
garments.how: upper cloth over one shoulder or both, loose, never pinned

garments.name: kāyabandha
garments.how: a sash or woven band at the waist holding the antarīya

garments.name: stanapaṭṭa
garments.how: a wrapped breast-band — NOT a stitched blouse, which is centuries later

garments.name: valkala / ajina
garments.how: bark cloth or deerskin, coarse, undyed, wrapped
garments.note: Vālmīki names bark cloth for forest life.

garments.name: cīra
garments.how: the rough cloth of renunciation — the garment that makes Ayodhyā unbearable to look at

register.king_at_court: fine cotton, near-white, dyed upper cloth with a woven border; ankle length
register.queen: fine cotton or silk, dyed, bordered; more cloth, more fall
register.ascetic: ochre or undyed; often one cloth only
register.brahmin_minister: cream or undyed white, upper cloth, restrained
register.rakshasa: MEMO REQUIRED — dress must not be used to mark monstrousness

forbidden: synthetic black as a fashion colour

never: sari pleated in the modern nivi style

ornament.principle: Drawn from what stone reliefs actually show — Bharhut, Sanchi, Amaravati — not from later jewellery. Gold gleams; it does not glitter.

forms.name: kuṇḍala
forms.who: almost everyone of rank, men and women
forms.note: Heavy enough to pull and lengthen the lobe. The signature Indian ornament of this period and the single fastest way to get the look right.

forms.name: hāra / niṣka
forms.note: flat gold collar or twisted torque

forms.name: keyūra / aṅgada
forms.note: armlet on the upper arm, above the bicep — inferred from the relief record (Bharhut). No loaded text in this workspace names it.

forms.name: kaṅkaṇa / valaya
forms.who: women in numbers, men one or two

forms.name: mekhalā
forms.note: girdle of linked plates or beads at the hip

forms.name: nūpura
forms.note: heavy anklets — a SOUND cue as much as an image. Hearing them precede a woman entering is period-correct and free.

forms.name: mukuṭa / kirīṭa
forms.note: a low band or modest crest — NOT a European peaked crown

forms.name: rudrākṣa
forms.note: seed beads, worn plain, never displayed

forms.name: yajñopavīta
forms.note: sacred thread over the left shoulder

forms.name: tilaka
forms.note: sandal paste or vermilion; small, not a pattern

forms.name: flowers
forms.note: real flowers as ornament — a class and season marker, not decoration

never: anything that glitters rather than gleams

body.principle: Indian faces, in their real variety. Not one face lightened or sharpened toward a European mean, and not one regional type standing for a subcontinent.

faces.requirement: Features from the actual range of the subcontinent — nose bridges that vary, eye shapes that vary, jaw and cheek structures that vary. A court should look like a place people came to from different regions, because it was.
forbidden: a single beauty standard applied to every face
narrowed or sharpened features to read 'noble'
broadened features to read 'lowly' — this is caste and race coding and we do not do it
wanted: pores, oil sheen, sun damage where a life has been lived outdoors
age in the neck and hands, not only the face

complexion.method: Locked as albedo and undertone, never judged from rendered pixels — the same skin reads differently under a lamp and a morning shaft.
complexion.range: The full South Asian range, mid-brown through deep brown, warm and olive undertones. Variation across a crowd is the point.
prohibited_absolutely: lightening at any stage, for any reason
lighting a face paler than its lock
fair = good, dark = evil coding of any kind

hair.men: long, oiled, bound in a knot or tied back; beards on elders and ascetics
hair.women: long, oiled, braided or coiled, flowers worked in. Loose hair means grief or violence and is never neutral.
hair.ascetics: jaṭā — matted, piled; ash on the skin
hair.boys: kākapakṣa — the side-locks. TEXTUAL: the spine calls Rāma kākapakṣadhara at the moment he is asked for. This is the clearest signal in the whole arc that he is a child, and it must be visible.

body.bodies: Real. Soft where age softens, hard where work hardens. Feet bare and dusty on every road. Hands that have done something.
never: everyone the same height and build

light.principle: One source, always motivated by something in frame.
sources: high lattice openings — long bars across stone
brass oil lamps — small, warm, close
open sky — hard and high at noon, raking at dawn

grade.saturation: restrained; colour comes from dyed cloth, not from the grade
grade.grain: film grain on every frame — generated images are too clean and read as fake without it

weapons.principle: Indian forms. The silhouette is the tell — a European cruciform hilt destroys a frame instantly.

forms.name: dhanuṣ
forms.what: bow — recurved, wood and horn, UNSTRUNG at rest, strung only to use

forms.name: khaḍga
forms.what: sword — Indian blade profile, leaf or straight with a broadening tip

forms.name: gadā
forms.what: mace — heavy head on a shaft

forms.name: jyā
forms.what: bowstring — its SOUND is a weapon in itself; Rāma twangs it and the forest empties

forms.name: godhāṅgulitrāṇa
forms.what: the archer's finger guard of guana skin — Dutt names it at the departure

astras.what: Divine weapons, named in the text and given to Rāma in arc 9.
astras.staging: An astra is a MANTRA, not a prop. The effect is in what happens, not in a shining object in a hand.

objects.principle: Brass, copper, clay, wood, leaf. Everything shows use.
everyday: brass standing oil lamps with a shallow dish and single wick
ritual: the sacrificial post (yūpa) — carved, wrapped in cloth, garlanded

types.name: city
types.reads_as: packed earth streets, timber and plaster buildings, water tanks, gardens within walls, rammed-earth and brick wall with timber gates

types.name: river
types.reads_as: wide, shallow, sandy banks, earth-and-stone ghats, timber boats

types.name: dry forest
types.reads_as: thorn, bare branches, hard shadow, dust. SILENT rather than lush.

types.name: deep forest
types.reads_as: tall trees, closed canopy, green shade, still air

types.name: hermitage
types.reads_as: a clearing, thatched huts, a fire altar, cattle, students

types.name: sea and island
types.reads_as: Sundara and Yuddha — its own memo

never: rainforest vines where the text means dry forest
anything that reads as fantasy wilderness

list: horses — Indian breeds, smaller, not warmbloods
elephants with cloth and rope, not showy caparison
krauñca birds (Bāla 2) — the sarus crane, and the pair matters
never: fantasy beasts where the text means an animal

crowds.principle: Individuals, always. Different ages, builds, complexions, dress conditions. A crowd reacts as several people, never as one.
never: a wall of extras facing camera

sound.principle: Recorded, never library. Library foley is Western foley — boots, leather, hinged doors — and audiences feel it without naming it.
palette: bare feet on stone and packed earth
never: library crowd walla in any language but ours

forbidden: anything Mughal, Rajput-palace, Victorian or fantasy-castle
anything that glitters rather than gleams
anything that reads as fantasy wilderness
rainforest vines where the text means dry forest
sari pleated in the modern nivi style
